ordered_diagnoses: Sjögren's Syndrome with Central Nervous System Involvement

s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent episodes of neurological deficits with evidence of inflammation and white matter changes
salient_findings: Mild headache and right facial droop
Extensive white matter changes on MRI
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level
key_facts: History of well-controlled hypertension and hyperlipidemia
On methotrexate and sulfasalazine treatment
Developed mild aphasia and confusion lasting several hours
Right leg weakness resolved within 2 days
Presented with mild headache and right facial droop
Neurological examination revealed paraphasic errors and word-finding difficulty
Mild right nasolabial flattening and bilateral upgoing plantars
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level
High titer of cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody
CSF analysis showed 12/µL white blood cell count and 4 oligoclonal bands
MRI Brain showed extensive white matter changes with enhancement along the arachnoid surface

shortlist: Sjögren's Syndrome with Central Nervous System Involvement

shortlist.label: Multiple Sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent episodes of neurological deficits with evidence of inflammation and white matter changes

shortlist.label: Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder
shortlist.why_kept: Optic neuritis and spinal cord lesions are common, but the presence of oligoclonal bands and white matter changes on MRI support this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Primary Central Nervous System Vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Inflammation and white matter changes on MRI, along with the presence of elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level

shortlist.label: Sjögren's Syndrome with Central Nervous System Involvement
shortlist.why_kept: High titer of cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody and presence of oligoclonal bands in CSF analysis

shortlist.label: Neurosarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level, along with the presence of lymphocytes and plasma cells on brain biopsy

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of relapsing neurological symptoms, such as mild aphasia, confusion, right leg weakness, and right facial droop, along with the presence of 4 oligoclonal bands in the CSF and extensive white matter changes on MRI, are characteristic of Multiple Sclerosis.

rejected.label: Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and MRI findings do not specifically indicate involvement of the optic nerve or spinal cord, which are typical of Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder.

rejected.label: Primary Central Nervous System Vasculitis
rejected.why: The brain biopsy did not show evidence of vasculitis, and the patient's symptoms and imaging findings are not typical of this condition.

rejected.label: Sjögren's Syndrome with Central Nervous System Involvement
rejected.why: While the patient has a high titer of cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, the clinical presentation and imaging findings are more consistent with Multiple Sclerosis than Sjögren's Syndrome.

rejected.label: Neurosarcoidosis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms, imaging findings, and biopsy results do not indicate granulomatous inflammation or other characteristic features of Neurosarcoidosis.
